Quantum Darwinism 
Wojciech Hubert Zurek 
Theory Division, MS B213, LANL Los Alamos, NM, 87545, U.S.A. 
(Dated: October 15, 2008) 
Quantum Darwinism - proliferation, in the environment, of multiple records of selected states of 
the system (its information-theoretic progeny) - explains how quantum fragility of individual state 
can lead to classical robustness of their multitude. 
As with many an old mystery , quantum measurement 
problem is celebrated with reverence reserved for myster­
ies of faith. Claims of progress are regarded as sacrilege. 
Yet, there was progress in the last quarter century or so. 
This is its brief review with a focus on one recent advance 
- quantum Darwinism. 
Quantum principle of superposition implies that any 
combination of quantum states is also a legal state. This 
seems to be in conflict with everyd ay reality: States we 
encounter are localized. Classical objects can be either 
here or there, but never both here and there. Yet, because
